overall: The AG found the Fairhaven Board of Health violated the Open Meeting Law by posting the June 11 notice late, approving seven sets of minutes untimely, and failing to take roll calls and announce a remote member on June 11; other allegations were rejected or declined.

allegations.summary: Not alleged by complainants: the Board's June 11 meeting notice was allegedly posted less than 48 hours before the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Although not raised in a complaint, we find that the Board did not post notice 48 hours prior to the June 11 meeting, which was a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the June 11 reorganization was not listed on the notice, or was insufficiently described.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the topic as listed on the notice sufficiently identified the discussion that occurred and therefore did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the 'Invoices/Other Business' sub-topics on the June 18 notice were insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board did that here as the notice listed five specific topics under

allegations.summary: Complaints that the July 9, July 16, and July 28 notices were vague and lacked descriptive information, without identifying specific topics.
allegations.key_passage: Complainants must allege violations with a degree of specificity, as our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies based on generalized allegations.

allegations.summary: Complaints that the Board discussed the Health Agent's personal health information in open session, alleging HIPAA violations.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, the allegations in these two complaints regarding a violation of HIPAA would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the chair allowed a Board of Selectmen member to speak during the June 18 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The law permits the Chair of the Board to decide who may speak at a meeting and for how long.

allegations.summary: Complaint that topics tabled on June 11 were omitted from the June 18 and later notices.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by not including topics on a subsequent notice or deciding not to discuss such topics at a subsequent meeting after having tabled the same topics at a previous meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Board did not read the findings of an Open Meeting Law violation, or read a submitted violation, into the record.
allegations.key_passage: In addition, the Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body discuss

allegations.summary: Complaints that the chair and vice chair, a quorum, deliberated outside the June 11 and June 18 meetings.
Complaints that the Board failed to timely approve minutes of meetings from May 28 through August 6.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve these minutes in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complaints that the Board discussed the Health Agent's medical matters and complaints against the Health Inspector in open session rather than executive session.
allegations.key_passage: As such, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to meet in executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the Board failed to conduct roll call votes at its June 11 meeting, when one member participated remotely.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to announce the name of the member who was participating remotely and by failing to conduct roll call votes during the June 11 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint that the chair failed to announce the name of the remotely participating member at the start of the June 11 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to announce the name of the member who was participating remotely and by failing to conduct roll call votes during the June 11 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaints that roll calls were not taken and remote-participation statements were not read at the June 18, July 9, July 16, July 28, and August 6 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Because no Board members participated remotely in these five meetings, the Board was not required to conduct votes by roll call or announce the names of members participating remotely.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law; a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the law, and caution the Board that a similar, future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation of the law.
